newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PFI hopes to avoid further value falls.
newsitem.headline: PFI hopes to avoid further value falls.

text.p: Property investment company Property for Industry Ltd said on Wednesday it was now more confident that it would not have to incur further reductions in portfolio value following a NZ$1.9 million write-down in June.
Directors said in June that further reductions could occur unless there was an improvement in economic conditions and/or the interest rate environment.
But Chairman Allan Lockie said they were now more confident that further losses would not occur.
Property for Industry earlier announced a nine-month net profit of NZ$2.1 million.
Net profit before the $1.9 million unrealised writedown was $4.07 million and Lockie said the company was on track to achieve its full-year budgeted forecast of $5.5 million after tax.
Property for Industry received $29.6 million from a successful rights issue this month and it said this enabled it to continue its acquisition strategy to take advantage of some yield weakness.
Most recently, properties have been acquired at yields in excess of 11 percent.
"The current indications of a better interest rate environment confirms the strategy the company has adopted and should benefit the value of Property for Industry's portfolio," Lockie said.
